title: checkout-api p99 spike, again — night of 2026-10-08

messages.content: checkout-api p99 is climbing again: 3.4s at the 99th percentile on POST /checkout since 02:05 UTC, and the first 504s are arriving. Same shape as the incident a couple of weeks ago — pods idle, redis unhappy, nightly reconciliation window. What did we actually change last time, and is that fix still holding?

content.text: Same symptom shape as last time, so start from the same two places: the API pods, then Redis.
Starting where the earlier incident started: are the API pods saturated this time?

content.text: Pods idling at ~180m again, exactly like the last incident — the stall is upstream of the process, so the deploy is not the story. Confirming the deploy anyway before I go further, because "it started at 02:05" invites that assumption.

input.command: kubectl -n checkout rollout history deploy/checkout-api | tail -3

content.text: Nothing shipped in six days, so the 02:05 start has to come from the workload, not the code. Redis client counts are the obvious next check.

content.text: connected_clients is pinned at 2048 against a maxclients of 2048, and 1187 of them are blocked. That looks like the ceiling we raised at the end of the last incident — so the change bought headroom and something has refilled it. I do not remember the reconciler details from that session well enough to guess at which pool is leaking again.

content.text: Those two sockets have been open and idle for nearly four hours — long-lived, which points at a pool holding connections rather than request traffic. Before I re-derive the last incident from scratch, I want its actual findings: which pool, what the cap was changed to, and what was left open. Pulling the earlier session's context in instead of guessing.
